newsitem.title: USA: Niagara Mohawk Power to refuel nuke plant.
newsitem.headline: Niagara Mohawk Power to refuel nuke plant.

text.p: Niagara Mohawk Power Corp said Tuesday it had removed one of its nuclear plants from service for refueling.
The company said it had removed a plant called Nine Mile Point One in Scriba, which had completed its 700-day operating cycle.
It said it would take about five weeks to refuel the 613-megawatt plant, replenishing one third of its 532 fuel bundles.
The company said it will hire more than 850 people including carpenters, steamfitters, electricians and laborers to help in the refueling.
It said the plant had its most productive cycle in its 27-year history, achieving a 92-percent capacity factor and generating 9.4 million megawatt-hours of electricity.
The plan was at its most productive due to reduced down time and improvements in plant equipment efficiency, it said.
The average annual capacity factor for U.S. plants is about 78 percent, it added.
